key_insight: Functional, low-overlap subnetworks inside an LLM can be isolated and selectively updated to reduce catastrophic forgetting during continual learning.
engineering_relevance: This offers a parameter- and optimizer-efficient way to adapt large models to new tasks while preserving prior capabilities, which is valuable for long-horizon deployed AI systems.
method: Use gradient-attribution profiling to identify cognition-associated functional subnetworks with minimal mutual overlap.
Route each training example to its corresponding subnetwork and restrict weight/optimizer updates to those selected regions.
Analyze subspace overlap and principal angles to verify representation preservation after localized updates.
evidence_signal: On 1.4 million sequential instructions, CiMEO achieved the best average performance across five generative benchmarks spanning programming, exam-style tasks, and mathematical reasoning, while reducing forgetting.
watch_item: Subnetwork routing and attribution-based localization may be sensitive to task distribution and model architecture, so transferability and routing overhead should be validated before deployment.
paper_title: Functional Subnetwork Localization for Efficient Continual Learning in Large Language Models
